messages:
sasha: heads-up — CI is failing in the paged-attention kernel link step after the toolchain bump to gcc-13 in the build image. linker error below from the failing job:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /workspace/runtime/attn/paged/libpaged.so: relocation R_X86_64_32 against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
mike_r: can you paste the exact docker image + bazel command to repro?
sasha: repro command is the same CI job: `bazel build //runtime/kernels:paged_attn --config=ci-image` — image is `registry.internal/redwood/ci-builder:bookworm-gcc13-2026-03-01`
build-bot: CI job https://ci.internal/job/eng-runtime/4876 failed on step "link libpaged.so" — log saved at artifacts/4876/paged-link.log
ana: quick thought — we've seen this when the builder uses ld.gold vs the packaging pipeline expecting ld.bfd. ld.gold can perform relaxations that expose non-PIC relocations. try forcing -fPIC on the paged kernel build and see if link succeeds.
jordan: also saw performance oddities after the gcc bump. microbench on fused-attn: median latency (seq=1024, batch=8) before gcc13 = 4.2ms, after gcc13 = 5.8ms. 99.9th tail from 18ms -> 42ms. KV-cache churned more on the new build, causing CPU stalls.
mike_r: those numbers are huge. do you have perf / hotspots?
jordan: yes — sampled stack shows a lot more page-fault/fixups inside dynamic reloc handling, and futex waits around global constructors for some kernels. attaching a short perf snippet:
```
# perf top (after gcc13 build)
  12.3%  ld-2.35.so  [.] _dl_fixup
   8.7%  libpthread.so.0 [.] __futex_wait
   6.1%  libpaged.so [.] paged_attn_compute
```
sasha: i repro'd locally by running the same container. switching to an older builder image (gcc-12 + ld.bfd) the link succeeds and perf numbers go back close to previous baseline. so this looks like a toolchain+linker ABI interaction not a logic regression.
perf-bot: benchmark artifact uploaded: https://benchmarks.internal/runs/2026-03/paged-kernel-gcc13-vs-gcc12 — diff includes latency histograms and kv-cache hit/miss counts.
nana: proposed immediate mitigations:
  - pin CI builder images for paged/fused kernels to gcc-12 (short-term)
  - add matrix build in CI to include gcc-12+ld.bfd and gcc-13+ld.gold to catch regressions earlier
  - force -fPIC on kernel shared objects during packaging to avoid relocation type errors
  - add small benchmark step in packaging CI to run a quick fused/paged latency smoke test (seq=512/1024)
mike_r: agree. also curious if LTO or visibility flags changed in the new image. can we diff CFLAGS from the two images?
sasha: i dumped `gcc -v` and `readelf -h` from both images and posted to the job artifacts. short dockerfile snippet for the failing image:
```Dockerfile
FROM debian:bookworm
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential gcc-13 g++-13 binutils-gold
ENV CC=gcc-13 CXX=g++-13
```
jordan: note — the binutils gold vs bfd difference alone can change symbol relaxation/PLT/GOT layout which feeds into TLB pressure at runtime. that matches the perf signals.
sasha: i'll open ENGRT-1234 to track this (title: paged/fused-attn: toolchain/linker-induced link failures and perf regression). assigning to @mike_r and adding steps to reproduce + perf artifacts. :eyes:
mike_r: will take it. i'll push a CI change to add gcc-12 image and a temporary bypass to pin packaging to gcc-12 while we investigate.
build-bot: created release-blocking label on job 4876 per policy.
nana: one final note — we'll want to validate that adding -fPIC doesn't materially affect performance; sometimes PIC can slow tight kernels. include that in the smoke test matrix.
sasha: noted. leaving checklist in the ticket and will update the PR with the CI matrix change. :thumbsup:
